## Overview

`mfrmr` provides high-speed C++ estimation, person scoring, diagnostics,
`RajuSA-Welch` pairwise bias / DFF screening, color-vision-safe `ggplot2`
visualizations, and generalizability analysis for Many-Facet Rasch Measurement
(`RSM`, `PCM`, and 1-/2-family `GPCM`). For end-to-end tidy pipelines and APA /
rater-feedback report generation, pair `mfrmr` with the companion `tidymfrm`
package.

## 1. Connectivity Audit and Fast C++ Estimation (`RSM`, `PCM`, and `GPCM`)

Each row of `example_core` represents one person's rating by a rater on an
analytic rubric criterion (`Score` 1 to 4):

```{r}
library(mfrmr)

ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
head(ratings, 4)

conn <- check_mfrm_connectivity(
  ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score"
)
conn$connected
conn$n_subsets
```

An assessment team may ask whether the same category steps work for every
criterion, and whether allowing different discrimination changes the fit.
The RSM shares steps across criteria; the PCM gives each criterion its own
steps; the GPCM additionally estimates criterion discrimination. Fit all three
by marginal maximum likelihood (`MML`) to the same ratings, with the same
fixed standard-normal ability distribution and 31-point integration rule.
These common settings make their nested likelihood comparisons interpretable.
`person_score = "WLE"` chooses Warm's score for reporting persons; it does not
change the MML calibration likelihood.

```{r}
fit_rsm <- fit_mfrm(
  ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  model = "RSM",
  method = "MML",
  person_score = "WLE"
)
print(fit_rsm)
fit_rsm$facets[, c("Facet", "Level", "Estimate", "ModelSE", "RealSE", "FairM", "InfitMnSq")]

fit_pcm <- fit_mfrm(
  ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  model = "PCM",
  step_facet = "Criterion",
  method = "MML"
)

fit_gpcm <- fit_mfrm(
  ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  model = "GPCM",
  step_facet = "Criterion",
  slope_facet = "Criterion",
  spec = list(gpcm_mml_identification = "fixed_standard_normal"),
  control = list(quad_points = 31L)
)
fit_gpcm$slopes[, c("Facet", "Level", "Estimate", "ModelSE")]
comparison <- anova(fit_rsm, fit_pcm, fit_gpcm)
comparison$lrt
```

Read each likelihood-ratio test as evidence about the restrictions removed
between two models. A small p-value supports relaxing those restrictions under
the likelihood assumptions; it does not establish practical importance or
validate the more complex model. Inspect parameter estimates, uncertainty and
residual diagnostics before choosing a model. Ineligible comparisons return no
LRT table and explain the reason in `comparison$comparison_basis`.

In this example, the RSM-to-PCM p-value is
`r format.pval(comparison$lrt$pValue[1], digits = 3)`, whereas the
PCM-to-GPCM p-value is `r format.pval(comparison$lrt$pValue[2], digits = 3)`.
At an illustrative 5% threshold, the data support criterion-specific steps,
with little evidence here for the additional discrimination parameters.
This is a model-comparison result for these ratings, not a recommendation to
use PCM for every rubric.

Check `summary(fit_rsm)$readiness` before interpreting intervals. Optimizer
convergence means that its stopping rule was met. Readiness additionally checks
the implemented connectivity, information-matrix and boundary conditions; it
does not establish model fit or nominal finite-sample coverage. Sparse ratings,
rare categories and dependence among ratings can still affect uncertainty.

Use standard S3 methods for a supported prediction scenario and calibration
intervals:

```{r}
predict(
  fit_rsm,
  newdata = data.frame(theta = c(-1, 0, 1), Rater = "R01", Criterion = "Content"),
  type = "response"
)
confint(fit_rsm, component = "facets")

plot(fit_rsm, type = "wright", palette = "okabe_ito")
plot(fit_gpcm, type = "slopes", palette = "monochrome")
```

Positive rater estimates indicate greater severity, and positive criterion
estimates indicate greater difficulty on the model's logit scale. The facet
intervals describe calibration uncertainty. Predictions above condition on the
specified ability and calibrated facet levels; they are not prediction
intervals for a new person's observed score. See `?fit_mfrm` and `?confint.mfrm_fit`
for identification, supported interval types and their limitations.

## 2. High-Speed Batch Replications

`mfrm_batch_fit()` executes Monte Carlo or bootstrap replications inside C++
worker threads without R interpreter overhead:

```{r}
set.seed(42)
rep_scores <- replicate(5L, sample(1:4, nrow(ratings), replace = TRUE))
batch_summary <- mfrm_batch_fit(
  ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  score_matrix = rep_scores,
  method = "CML",
  model = "RSM",
  rating_min = 1,
  rating_max = 4,
  threads = 1L,
  return_fits = FALSE
)
batch_summary
```
